title: Partition presubmit runner across lanes and add dependency-refresh orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline has become a major contributor to developer feedback latency. Large monolithic presubmit jobs (lint + unit + integration + e2e) amplify queue times and make dependency-refresh PRs (dependabot and internal) spike CI load, causing noisy failures and long iteration cycles. This PR introduces two complementary changes: (1) a partitioned presubmit runner that routes changes to lane-specific job sets (fast, standard, integration) to reduce median feedback time and deconflict heavy test jobs; and (2) a dependency-refresh orchestrator that schedules and staggers dependency bump PRs to avoid CI thundering herds and to allow rolling canary validation of larger upgrades.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add a presubmit router action (actions/presubmit-router) that labels PRs with presubmit-lane based on file globs, change size, and modified services. The router is implemented as a small TypeScript GitHub Action and a config file at .github/presubmit-lanes.yaml.
- Split the monorepo GH workflow into three lanes: presubmit-fast.yml, presubmit-standard.yml, presubmit-integration.yml. Each workflow runs a subset of jobs and reuses composite actions to keep duplication low.
- Introduce a lightweight orchestrator service (tools/dep-refresh/orchestrator) that sequences dependency bump PRs. The orchestrator uses a lease mechanism (Redis) and posts status checks to coordinate canary runs and staged rollouts.
- Refactor existing lint/test scripts (scripts/ci/*) to accept lane hints and to produce lane-aware artifacts/annotations.
- Add new observability hooks: CI lane metrics (prometheus/meter tags) and a short-run smoke test that runs when dep-refresh orchestrator promotes a PR to canary.
- Tests and infra: unit tests for the router and orchestrator, integration test harness for lane routing logic, and updated action metadata.

Commits (summary):
- feat(presubmit): add presubmit router action and config
- ci(workflows): split presubmit into fast/standard/integration lanes
- feat(deps): add dep-refresh orchestrator service with lease logic
- refactor(ci): make scripts lane-aware, add lane annotations to test runners
- test(ci): add unit/integration tests for router and orchestrator
- docs: document presubmit lanes and rollout plan in docs/dev/presubmit.md

Changed files (representative):
- .github/actions/presubmit-router/action.yml
- .github/actions/presubmit-router/index.ts
- .github/presubmit-lanes.yaml
- .github/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml
- .github/workflows/presubmit-standard.yml
- .github/workflows/presubmit-integration.yml
- tools/dep-refresh/orchestrator/main.go
- scripts/ci/run-tests.sh (refactor to accept LANE env var)
- docs/dev/presubmit.md
- ci/metrics/presubmit_lanes.prom (meter tpl)

Testing and validation:
- Local unit test coverage added for router and orchestrator: 82%/78% respectively.
- Staging runs: executed against the staging org (redwood-staging) with a synthetic mix of 200 small PRs and 20 dependency PRs. Median presubmit latency improved from 9m45s to 2m30s for fast-lane PRs and from 18m to 7m for standard-lane PRs. Integration-lane queue depth reduced by ~60% under load.
- Dep-refresh orchestrator: successfully sequenced a batch of 12 dependency bumps; canary promotion prevented two regressions by isolating them to the canary cohort.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy router action and workflows to staging and enable presubmit-lane labeling behind feature flag (gh:presubmit-router=on).
2) Run canary on 10% of dev teams for 48h; monitor CI latencies, failure modes, and lane label accuracy.
3) Gradually enable for all, then enable dep-refresh orchestrator in a dry-run mode for 72h before authorizing automatic promotions.

Notes / alternatives considered:
- We evaluated single-workflow sharding via test slicing but found lane-level partitioning simpler to reason about and better aligned with developer expectations.
- We considered using GitHub queue API (if available), but opted for an independent router to keep control and observability.

Related: ENG-9876 (presubmit latency initiative), ENG-10021 (dep refresh safety improvements).

CI checks summary: unit-tests (pass), integration-smoke (pass), lint (pass), action-build (pass), staging-canary (pass).

Maya Chen: addressed the async/await nit; pushed a follow-up commit to normalize error handling
Priya Nair: Can we ensure the orchestrator lease fallback is resilient to transient Redis failures? Also requested a short-circuit for manual takeover in docs
Maya Chen: added exponential backoff + circuit breaker in orchestrator; documented manual takeover steps in docs/dev/presubmit.md
Ethan Brooks: Approved after verifying the staging canary metrics and seeing the median latency improvements in the perf run

Maintainer (A. Singh): Squash-merged after approvals and green CI; noted a follow-up task to tune lane heuristics (ENG-10100)
release_notes:
- Introduce presubmit lane partitioning (fast/standard/integration) to reduce developer feedback latency.
- Add presubmit-router GitHub Action and configuration file.
- Add dependency-refresh orchestrator to sequence and canary dependency bump PRs.
- Refactor CI scripts to be lane-aware and add lane metrics.

notes: This PR intentionally keeps the router heuristics conservative for initial rollout (prefer explicit path globs and small-change thresholds). Follow-ups will iterate towards more aggressive auto-classification.
ci_pipeline_snapshot: presubmit-fast: 3 jobs (lint, unit, smoke); presubmit-standard: 6 jobs (lint, unit, integration-smoke, build-matrix); presubmit-integration: 4 heavy jobs (integration, e2e, cross-service-contracts)
perf_impact_summary: Staging synthetic run: median fast-lane presubmit 9m45s -> 2m30s, standard 18m -> 7m. Integration lane queue depth down ~60% under same load.
